terminal.description: A shell in your workspace where the demo tries your stamp card, memoize and once helpers.

tasks.title: A stamp card that remembers
tasks.description:
Implement `createStampCard(goal)` under `// Task 1` in `src/helpers.js`. It returns a card object with two methods:

- `stamp()` adds one stamp. When the card reaches `goal` stamps it returns `true` (a free candle) and the card starts again from `0`. Otherwise it returns `false`.
- `stamps()` returns how many stamps the card holds right now.

Every card keeps its own count.
nextSteps: Return an object with `stamp` and `stamps` methods that use it.
Handle the goal: return `true` and start again from 0.
Run `node src/demo.js` and read the first line.
hints: The count has to survive between calls to `stamp()` but must not be shared between cards. Where can a variable live so that is true?
A `let` inside `createStampCard` is created fresh on every call, and the methods you return can still read and change it.
In `stamp()`, add one first, then compare with `goal`. Only when they match do you reset and return true.

tasks.title: Remember slow answers
tasks.description:
Implement `memoize(fn)` under `// Task 2` in `src/helpers.js`. It returns a new function of one argument that gives the same result as `fn`, but calls `fn` at most once per distinct argument and reuses the saved result after that.

- arguments are distinct the way a `Map` sees them, so `1` and `'1'` are different
- results like `0`, `''` and `undefined` are saved too
- every memoized function has its own memory
nextSteps: Return a function that looks up its argument first.
Call `fn` only when the argument has not been seen, and save the result.
Run the demo and check that `lookups` is 2.
hints: This is the same trick as the stamp card: a variable inside the outer function that the returned function keeps using.
A plain object turns every key into a string. A `Map` keeps `1` and `'1'` apart.
Decide with `cache.has(arg)`, not with whether `cache.get(arg)` is truthy. A saved 0 is still saved.

tasks.title: Only once
tasks.description:
Implement `once(fn)` under `// Task 3` in `src/helpers.js`. It returns a new function. The first time that function is called, it calls `fn` with the same arguments and returns `fn`'s result. Every later call returns that first result again without calling `fn`, whatever arguments it gets.

This must hold even when `fn` returned `undefined`.
nextSteps: Keep two variables inside `once`: whether `fn` ran, and what it returned.
Return a function that takes any number of arguments with `...args`.
On the first call run `fn(...args)` and remember both things.
Run the demo and check that only one welcome email was sent.
hints: Two pieces of memory are needed here, not one. What would go wrong if you only kept the result?
Rest parameters (`...args`) collect every argument, and spread (`fn(...args)`) passes them on unchanged.
Use a boolean flag to decide whether to call `fn`. Checking `result === undefined` breaks when `fn` returns undefined.
